title: Demonstrate an understanding of the role and requirements of water in plants

lessons.title: Why plants need water
lessons.html:
Why plants need water

Water is life for plants. Most of a plant is water. A soft lettuce leaf or a petunia stem is almost all water. Without water a plant wilts, then dies.

What water does in a plant

  • Keeps the plant firm. Water fills the cells and makes leaves and soft stems stand up. When there is not enough water, the plant goes floppy. This is wilting.
  • Carries food. Plant food from the soil, such as fertiliser, must dissolve in water before the roots can take it up.
  • Helps make food. Leaves use water, sunlight and air to make sugar. This is photosynthesis.
  • Cools the plant. Leaves let water out into the air, like sweating. This cools the plant on hot days.

How water moves through the plant

  1. Fine roots take up water from the soil.
  2. Water moves up the stem in thin tubes.
  3. Water reaches the leaves.
  4. Most of it goes out through tiny holes under the leaves into the air. This is called transpiration.

Plants lose the most water when it is hot, sunny, dry and windy. On such days they need more water.

Signs of too little water

  • Wilting leaves, especially in the morning
  • Leaves curl, go dull or turn brown at the edges
  • Lawn turns grey-blue and footprints stay
  • Flowers and buds drop
  • Soil is dry and pulls away from the side of the pot

Note: some plants wilt a little in the hot afternoon and recover in the evening. If they are still wilted in the morning, they need water.

lessons.title: Different water needs and too much water
lessons.html:
Different water needs and too much water

Not all plants need the same water

PlantWater needWhy
Seedlings and new plantsHigh, oftenSmall roots, cannot reach deep water
Annual flowers and lawnsMedium to highShallow roots, fast growth
Established shrubs and treesLow to medium, deepDeep roots find water
Succulents and aloesLowStore water in thick leaves
Plants in potsHigherSmall amount of soil dries fast

Soil and water

  • Sandy soil lets water run through fast. It dries out quickly and needs water more often.
  • Clay soil holds water for a long time. Water it less often, and slowly, so water can soak in.
  • Compost and mulch help all soils hold water better.

Too much water

Roots also need air. If the soil is always wet, there is no air and roots rot. Signs of too much water:

  • Yellow lower leaves
  • Plant wilts even though the soil is wet
  • Soft, brown, smelly roots
  • Green slime or moss on the soil
  • Water standing in pots or beds

Make sure pots have drainage holes. Do not water if the soil is still wet.

Good water quality

Very salty water, or water with chemicals in it, can harm plants. Some borehole water is salty. Ask your team leader which water to use.

Saving water

Water is scarce in South Africa. Water at the right time, in the right amount, and use mulch.

Key points

  • Water keeps plants firm, carries food, helps make food and cools the plant.
  • Water moves from roots, up the stem, and out of the leaves.
  • Hot, dry, windy days make plants lose more water.
  • Different plants and soils need different amounts of water.
  • Too much water rots roots; roots need air too.
